extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO guidelines for how patent applications are processed, examined, classified, and reported in Korea, including examiner duties, amendment/reexamination rules, and IPC/CPC classification principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of Formal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Check whether an application meets formal requirements: capacity, representation, formality of the application, fees, and provisions on returning application documents under Article 11(1) of the Enforcement Rules of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary check is in principle carried out by the receiving office in the name of the Commissioner of KIPO; if the receiving office fails, an examiner may carry out further checks in the name of the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of Patent Classification (CPC, IPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign classification taking into consideration the invention as claimed to enable effective prior-art search and retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO adopts the IPC; CPC may be allocated (every application except PCT filed after Jan 2015 is allocated CPC and IPC automatically). Classification must be accurate and based on technical subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laying-open (Publication) of Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish the application in the Patent Gazette 18 months after filing (or earliest priority date if priority claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may request earlier publication; applications treated confidential may be excluded from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Examination Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is examined only when a request for examination is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person can request examination within 3 years from filing date (5 years for applications filed before 3.1.2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of Examination Order and Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Examinations proceed in the order of requests for examination; the purpose is to ensure the application meets substantive requirements of Article 46 or 62.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prime task of the examiner is substantive examination; if formality requirements are lacking, the examiner may invite correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Grounds for Rejection (Right to Respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a decision to reject under Article 62, the examiner shall notify the applicant of grounds for rejection to give chance to submit arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice is provided prior to issuance of the decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and Written Arguments by Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may submit arguments and file amendments to the specification or drawings in response to an examiner's notice within the period designated in Article 47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and arguments must be considered by the examiner in subsequent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination After Amendments/Arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: After taking into account amendments or arguments made by the applicant in reply to a rejection, the examiner should re-examine the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination is repeated considering applicant's responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Grant a Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner finds no grounds to reject the application, the examiner shall decide to grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant follows successful substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Officio Amendments on Grant
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a decision to grant, an examiner may amend obvious errors in the specification, drawings, or abstract ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall notify the applicant of the ex officio errors to be amended along with a certified copy of the decision to grant; the applicant can accept the amendment by the time for paying patent registration fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Reject when Applicant Fails to Overcome Grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after re-examination considering amendments/arguments, the examiner considers the applicant fails to overcome the rejection, the examiner shall issue a decision to reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the formal rejection step after opportunity to reply has been afforded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment and Request for Reexamination (Timing & Limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may amend specification/drawings and request reexamination within 30 days from receipt of a certified copy of the decision to reject, subject to statutory extension rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination request not allowed where a decision to reject was issued after reexamination or where a notice of appeal is filed. A request for reexamination deems the prior decision withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is made, the examiner shall consider any amendments and re-examine the application following the general examination procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination treats the earlier decision as withdrawn and repeats examination considering amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to Reject after Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If following reexamination the examiner still finds the grounds for rejection have not been overcome, the examiner shall decide to reject the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rejection after reexamination is formalized in a decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO shall designate a qualified examiner to examine patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or more examiners are designated for each IPC and one is designated as the primary examiner; Patent Examination Support Division appoints primary examiners at request of the director general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Examiner: Speed, Accuracy, Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall proceed with examination with speed and accuracy in accordance with the Patent Act and related provisions and shall examine independently based on legal and technical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opinions of supervisors may be taken into consideration; newly appointed examiners serve as assistant examiners for up to 1 year and then jointly with experienced examiners for an additional year (training requirements may shorten these periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation and Joint Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions involving convergence technologies or multiple technical aspects, the primary examiner may consult with other examiners in relevant sub-technical classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consultation is used, the primary examiner shall notify the applicant of the consultation, names of consulting examiners and reasons; documents are made under joint names while reporting is mainly by the primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation for Foreign-language Prior Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may consult other examiners with expertise in foreign languages (e.g., French, Chinese, Japanese, Spanish) to better understand prior art in those languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits more accurate prior-art assessment when documents are in foreign languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-level Joint Conference for Difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where unified rule application or judgment causes difficulty, a director general may convene a joint conference of more than 3 examiners for opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to resolve complex or contentious examination policy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of Confidentiality for Examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must maintain confidentiality regarding information acquired in official capacity and carry out examination duties with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents related to a patent application/examination shall not be carried out except for prior-art searches, digitization, or on-line remote performance. No responses to requests for expert opinion, testimony, or inquiries about contents of pending applications, examinations, trials, retrials, or decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on Change or Continuation of Examiner in Charge
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner transfers divisions after issuance of first office action, that examiner continues examination up to final decision; applications returned after revocation are examined by the same examiner unless justifiable reason for change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: when revoked and returned more than twice examiner may be changed; an examiner shall not be in charge of same IPC for 5 consecutive years except for expertise/efficiency; examiners with conflicts or insufficient experience are excluded from certain examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Reporting Obligations of Examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must report certain dispositions (allowance, rejection, refusal to enter amendment, grant decision, invalidation dispositions, notices of rejection/grant, reexamination decisions, patent term extension decisions, third office actions, etc.) to heads of team/division and upward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting requirements vary by examiner grade; examples provided when reporting may be exempted for junior/senior/chief examiners; grade determined by experience and training requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Authority Name for Examination-related Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prescribed due form for certain documents; if none designated use general document form per Instruction on Office Management; list attachments at end of document body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent examination shall be conducted in the name of the examiner in charge except for specific matters (e.g., Article 46 amendment requests, invalidation measures, returns, expedited examination); joint or consultation exams under joint names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification Assignment Must Reflect Essential Technical Subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent classification assignment must be made accurately based on the technical subject-matter of the invention, determined from claims in light of description and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification should be based on the essential contents of the claimed invention as a whole, not bound to formality such as category of invention; if claims unclear, use description/drawings; if claims and description differ, description matters are classified as additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main vs Sub-classification for Multiple Subject-matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple technical subject-matters exist, core technical subject-matter representing the claimed invention as a whole is main classification; others are sub-classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If difficult to separate core subject-matter or claim 1 is not under a prescribed group, classification sign of claim 1 may be referred to as main classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC General Rule: Function-oriented vs Application-oriented Assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine first whether a classification place is function-oriented or application-oriented and classify accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 'use' inventions with a single use and a relevant IPC place, that place is the basis; where IPC has no use place, function-oriented place becomes main classification with pertinent use as sub-classification. For function-oriented inventions, classify based on function; if no function place exists, classify by main use in the specification. Examples (valves) illustrate difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC Notation and Order in Patent Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents indicate IPC identification abbreviation, classification symbols/indexing code, and version in that order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification symbols describing invention information → additional information → indexing code; invention info in boldface, additional info in regular type, italic style for extension level; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Additional Information and Indexing Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information complements invention information and can be given by indexing codes or classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing codes are designated based on an indexing classification table categorized by technical functions (purpose, use, structure, material, manufacturing process, disposal, control measure, etc.) and help refine searchable technical subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Security / Confidential Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention requires confidentiality due to national security, this requirement shall be stated and treated according to special procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part VII, chapter 3 for details (referred to in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification Guidance for Specific Technical Subject Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for selecting classification place by technical subject: apparatus or method (prefer pertinent place for either), products (classify by product place or function/use), multistage processes/plants (classify by composition or output), specifics/parts (classify in apparatus place unless reusable across multiple apparatuses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no relevant place exists for apparatus, use method; if neither exist, use product place. For products with no place, use function-oriented place then use. For multistage compositions, classify by composition place or output; constituents may also receive individual classification where they have individual characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Original Application Classification for Related Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For divisional, converted, domestic/treaty priority claim, or later applications of lawful holder, identify original application's classification first and generally retain it as main classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only change when original classifications obviously fail to correspond to the later-filed application; prefer to keep original classification as main and designate newly granted classification as sub-classification.
